title: Signed login transcript (versioned)
$comment: Structural residue of the auth.transcript.* rules (P0-3, A3.1). The signed login transcript binds the fields that close cross-protocol replay and relying-party substitution (auth.transcript.bound-fields): a domain-separation tag, the auth contract, the authorization-server issuer and token endpoint, the required audience, the subject DID, the exact verification method id, a nonce, and a timestamp. Per the P0-4 canonical freeze the transcript is canonicalized with jcs-rfc8785 and all fields are strings (auth-grant.yaml, canon.number.safe-integer). Wire field names are snake_case, the JWT/OAuth convention for this artifact family (contrast the camelCase W3C-VC-lineage evidence structures). $defs are inlined (no cross-file $ref).

transcript_version.$comment: auth.transcript.bound-fields: the versioned wire contract is pinned, not a free string, so a transcript names exactly one schema version.

domain_separation_tag.$comment: auth.transcript.domain-separation: a fixed tag separates login from delegation; an arbitrary tag would not normatively close cross-protocol replay. Frozen literal (P0-3/P0-4), paired with identity.wire-variant-id's provin-wire-variant-v1 convention.

auth_contract_id.$comment: claims.login.contracts: which login contract this transcript is made under.

audience.$comment: auth.transcript.audience-required: a strict profile requires a non-empty audience; an empty-allowlist any-audience acceptance is rejected (semantic, pinned by vector).

verification_method.$comment: auth.grant.exact-method / auth.grant.kid-match: the absolute verification method id, identical to the JWS protected kid and the resolver-selected method.

timestamp.$comment: An RFC 3339 UTC instant as a string (canon.number.safe-integer: no numeric time fields).
